subject: EU → AU failover drill and egress audit for private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Suresh <rajiv@medcloud.io>, Helen O'Neill <helen.oneill@c2-int.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: EU → AU failover drill and egress audit for private VPC deployment

Hi Rajiv / Helen,

Following our architecture review last month, MedCloud's private VPC deployment will need a documented dry-run that demonstrates regional failover from our EU control plane into the Australia (AU) warm-standby site. The security and DPO teams asked for a short evidence package and a single tabletop + dry-run during the week of May 25th.

Scope we want to cover in the drill:
- Trigger and validate control-plane handoff (canary route -> standby)
- Confirm KMS key access mapping and ciphertext recovery in AU
- Egress gating: show that no customer data egresses to unexpected jurisdictions during failover
- Latency and SLO observation: show expected tail latency impact and rollback path

Ask from your side: please confirm the DPO's acceptance criteria (logs, attestation, timeframe) and whether any additional data processing addenda are needed before we run. For the engineering checklist, I'd like Redwood to provide: a network diagram focused on cross-region peering, an exported sample of our egress filter rules, and a short mapping of KMS key regions.

I've looped in Karthik to propose the technical runbook and Grace for observability readiness. If we can get the requested evidence uploaded to the Drive link below by May 20, we can lock the dry-run date.

Attachments (will upload separately): standby-network-diagram.pdf, kms-region-map.csv, egress-filter-sample.log

Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/Shared/MedCloud/Residency/EU-AU-DR-2026
HS reference: HS-12345678

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from the MedCloud side:

1) The DPO will want both (a) logs showing egress gate decisions for a 24h window around the test and (b) an attestation signed by Redwood that the warm-standby will only accept traffic for tenant IDs provisioned for AU locality. Can you confirm you can provide both?

2) For encryption: we need the list of KMS key alias names used in EU and the process for key access in AU (rekeying vs cross-region decrypt). High-level notes are fine — we don't need key material.

3) Timing: May 25 works from our calendar but preferred window is 00:00–04:00 UTC to minimize production impact. Would that align with your team's ops window?

Also tagging Helen from our compliance partner to confirm any extra contractual items.

Best,
Rajiv
Head of Platform Ops, MedCloud Health

Marissa / Rajiv —

I've dropped an initial runbook into the Drive folder (failover-runbook-v1.md). Summary highlights (short):

1) Preconditions (30m prior): confirm current routing table snapshot, BGP session health, and active KMS alias mappings.
2) Dry-run steps (60m):
   - Step 0: Acquire signed approval from MedCloud on the run window (we'll capture sign-off in the Drive file).
   - Step 1: Shift a single canary route for a low-traffic tenant to AU; observe connection path and KV cache priming.
   - Step 2: Validate egress logs for that tenant for 1h window; run the egress gating verification script (attached sample).
   - Step 3: Exercise rollback and confirm the control plane remaps to EU route and stale KV cache invalidation.
3) Acceptance criteria:
   - No egress to non-approved regions during the 1h window (audit log + filter sample)
   - KMS decrypt success for the canary tenant in AU without exposing key material
   - Tail P95/P99 latency within agreed thresholds (we've allowed a 2x temporary uplift for canary)

Caveats and notes:
- Warm-standby will increase token-serving cost while KV priming happens — approximate uplift is ~15–30% for the hour depending on token volume. If cost needs a hard cap, tell us and we'll carve the canary to smaller tenant traffic.
- If DPO needs a signed attestation form, we can produce our standard residency attestation (I'll attach a template if required).

Proposed dry-run window: 2026-05-26 00:30–02:00 UTC. Rajiv, please confirm availability and DPO acceptance of the attestation approach; if accepted, we'll lock the date and run the tabletop two days prior.

Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
